articles.title: What does Met’s U-turn on John Galliano augur for him, the gala and Anna Wintour?
articles.summary: NYC’s elite figures, led by Julie Menin, made Wintour blink, and the designer who in 2011 had gone on a drunken antisemitic rant, bowed out of industry’s biggest event.
body: Did Anna Wintour, Vogue’s long-serving fashion titan and ringmaster of the annual Met Gala, meet her match in Julie Menin, the speaker of New York’s city council?

The museum is the crown jewel of the wealthy neighborhood and some residents hold significant sway at the institution, financially and in terms of the art they plan to bequeath to it. So when it was announced late in July on a Friday afternoon that Galliano would be the focus of the Met Gala next year, it left many stunned.

The designer, whose astonishing creativity as designer at Givenchy and later Dior in the 90s is not in question, had been videotaped in a Paris bar in 2011 abusing tourists in a drunken, antisemitic rant. “I love Hitler,”he slurred, and indicated their forebears should have been gassed.

Galliano was dispatched to rehab, sought corrective instruction from Jewish leaders and picked up a conviction for making hateful remarks about Jews and Asians. He got sober, apologized and made amends. He visited Auschwitz and gingerly resumed his career, though not at the top of a Parisian design house.
points: NYC’s elite figures, led by Julie Menin, made Wintour blink, and the designer who in 2011 had gone on a drunken antisemitic rant, bowed out of industry’s biggest event.

articles.title: Kardashian curves: M&S launches £28 bodysuit with exaggerated hip padding
articles.summary: The ‘hip boost’ aims to create hourglass silhouette, much like Kim Kardashian’s shapewear brand’s padded shorts. For decades shapewear has been used to compress and cinch. But now there is a sub-genre emerging. Rather than shrinking a silhouette, it aims to add inches.
body: This week M&S launched a bodysuit that features exaggerated padding at the hip allowing the wearer to create an hourglass shape, or at least the illusion of one.
Similar to how bra inserts, AKA chicken fillets, are used to add extra volume to breasts, the £28 “hip boost” features pockets on each side of the suit that allow the wearer to add in enhancing pads.

Charlotte Davies, the director of lingerie at the retailer, says the idea stemmed from customer interest in “solutions that offer subtle enhancement alongside everyday comfort and confidence”, with the trend being driven by the catwalks and celebrities. The hip booster’s predecessors at M&S include padded bum shorts “to give the wearer a curvy, contoured look” and stick-on nipples for “a realistic raised profile beneath clothing”.

Kim Kardashian’s shapewear brand, Skims, launched shorts with hip padding last year. Many users online claim such type of strategic padding can help minimise “hip dips” – a phrase used to describe the natural inward curves between the hipbone and thigh bone.
points: The ‘hip boost’ aims to create hourglass silhouette, much like Kim Kardashian’s shapewear brand’s padded shorts.

articles.title: ‘This is colonialism for clicks’: the influencers attempting to meet and film the world’s most isolated tribes
articles.summary: A new breed of adventurer is chasing internet fame by targeting uncontacted peoples. Critics say they are risking the wellbeing of these remote communities – and their own lives. He set out from the beach around midnight, packing his camera, a coconut and a can of Diet Coke.
body: After hours of motoring across the Bay of Bengal, his destination came into view: a low-lying island, narrowly separating sea and sky. With the sun now high above him, Polyakov cut the engine and set his GoPro to record. “So, the goal,” he said, squinting towards the blinding-white beach. “Introduce this Palaeolithic tribe to modernity … Let’s land on this bitch.”

Polyakov was nearing North Sentinel Island, part of the Andaman archipelago governed by India. Venturing within 5km (3 miles) is strictly prohibited, let alone setting foot on shore, and authorities routinely patrol the surrounding waters. But Polyakov saw himself as on a mission: to see – and, more importantly, film – the Indigenous people who live there.
points: A new breed of adventurer is chasing internet fame by targeting uncontacted peoples.
Critics say they are risking the wellbeing of these remote communities – and their own lives.

articles.title: ‘It struck me as a minimalist tableau’: Henk Stam’s best phone picture
articles.summary: The Dutch photographer was pleased to capture this suitably orange scene in some toilets in Rotterdam. ‘I must admit I was very sceptical of phone photography at first,” Henk Stam says. Sixty years ago, he received his first camera for his 11th birthday.
body: This photo was taken in Portlantis, a visitors’ centre in the Port of Rotterdam that opened in spring 2025. Stam spent his working life in Canada but was born in the Netherlands and returned there on retirement. With a friend from his photo club, he went to visit Portlantis on a Monday, but found it closed. “As we were leaving, we noticed a large tour bus arriving filled with teenagers,” he says. “We simply joined the slipstream as they entered; no one batted an eyelid.”

There was still construction work being done inside, and as Stam nipped to the toilet, he spotted this worker’s legs sticking out of a cubicle, toolbox at his side. “It struck me as a minimalist tableau. Here, the royal family are referred to as the House of Orange, national teams and fans wear orange, and we festoon our streets with orange flags during major events. But I found it odd one would colour the toilets orange.”

Stam had left his camera with his friend, so grabbed this shot on his phone instead. He returned to Portlantis a few months later. “This time entering legitimately,” he says. “But nothing I captured then matched the uniqueness of this moment.”

articles.title: The Best On-Court Style Moments Served at the 2026 U.S. Open
articles.summary: The 2026 U.S. Open is in full swing! With Naomi Osaka, Coco Gauff, and Venus Williams in play, don’t expect traditional tennis whites on the hard court.
body: Ready, set…style. The 2026 U.S. Open is in full swing in Queens, New York City, with the season already serveing up some thrilling,—and stylish—moments.

Serena Williams made her return with doubles partner Carlos Alcaraz, who was back in it after an injury that struck him out of this year’s Wimbledon. The duo sported some striking matching royal purple and black Nike kits. Roger Federer played a once-in-a-lifetime exhibition match at the Arthur Ashe Stadium with Lorenzo Musetti—and also launched a limited-edition version of On’s The Roger shoe —before absconding to Rhode Island to be inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame.

Across the next few days, we’ll see the likes of women’s world number one Aryna Sabalenka, Naomi Osaka, Coco Gauff, Venus Williams, Taylor Fritz, and more hit the Flushing Meadows hard court. The Williams sisters were at the forefront of subverting traditional tennis whites. Gauff debuted her latest New Balance x Miu Miu on the London grass, while Sabalenka is a Gucci face, Fritz is a Boss ambassador, and Novak Djokovic reps Lacoste.
points: With Naomi Osaka, Coco Gauff, and Venus Williams in play, don’t expect traditional tennis whites on the hard court.

articles.title: This Artist Bride’s Hand-Painted Danielle Frankel Dress Shaped the Aesthetic of Her Carmel Valley Wedding
articles.summary: Artist Mackenzie Cantor married entrepreneur Benjamin Taft in a garden wedding at the Carmel Valley Ranch, with the cream and pastel blue hues of the bride’s gown defining the palette of the wedding.
body: The ceremony took place at golden hour on the lawn of the Carmel Valley Ranch Resort. “Our chuppah was designed to be an architectural preview of the dinner space the guests would see later on in the evening,” shares Mackenzie. “It was a large structure, elevated on a stage with florals that wrapped around to match the surrounding nature.” As the ceremony began, “Canon in D” was played on a grand piano as a nod to Ben’s mother, who is a classical pianist. “When I came down the aisle, the pianist switched to my favorite song: ‘Accidentally in Love’ by Counting Crows,” says the bride.

The groom’s sister officiated the proceedings alongside Rabbi Peretz, who brought Jewish traditions into the ceremony. “Ben’s sister is like a second mom to him, since she is 12 years older and helped raise him, so it was very special to have her up there with us,” shares Mackenzie. Ben shares he felt very present and emotional throughout the ceremony. “Despite all our guests being there, it felt like Mackenzie and I were in our own little private bubble with just the two of us, my sister, and our rabbi,” he says. Adds the bride, “I couldn’t have asked for a better day.”
points: Artist Mackenzie Cantor married entrepreneur Benjamin Taft in a garden wedding at the Carmel Valley Ranch, with the cream and pastel blue hues of the bride’s gown defining the palette of the wedding.

articles.title: Kim Gordon and Suzanne Lindon on Film, Friendship, and Collaborating With Claire Denis for Miu Miu Women’s Tales
articles.summary: The actor and musician are premiering the latest chapter in Miu Miu’s ongoing short film series at Venice Film Festival—and shared the story behind the film with Vogue.
body: It’s a sunny spring day in Paris, and a young woman is in a mechanic’s workshop, tending to a retro silver Ford. She is checking the engine oil and polishing the bonnet, grease smeared across her cheek. She hops in the car and begins a flâneur-like odyssey around the city, where she undergoes a series of strange, lightly surreal encounters—helping a woman move an antique chair across the street, dropping off boxes of plants at a store—before approaching the famous Fontaine des Lions in the city’s 12th arrondissement, where a figure stands waiting.

She’s wearing an incongruously wintry outfit for this balmy weather—a trapper hat bedecked with embroidered crystals, an equally snug shearling-lined coat, knee-high boots—and carries bags with her, as if arriving for a stay with our unnamed protagonist. Then, she begins to walk towards the camera, and as you look more closely, you notice: is that… Kim Gordon?
points: The actor and musician are premiering the latest chapter in Miu Miu’s ongoing short film series at Venice Film Festival—and shared the story behind the film with Vogue.

articles.title: On Hulu’s ‘Furious’ and the Potent Fantasy of Revenge
articles.summary: “Furious” imagines a world in which the powerful can be made physically afraid of someone they once regarded as disposable. Its popularity may tell us less about women’s appetite for brutality than about our collapsing faith in systems of justice.
body: In the second episode of Furious, Hulu’s 2026 series about a survivor of childhood sex trafficking seeking revenge on the men who abused her, Catherine Grace (Lola Pettigrew) is standing in a kitchen, preparing raw chicken breasts, when a man at the edge of the frame begins commando crawling across the floor toward her.

He seizes her aggressively by the ankle, a move that in most stories would signal she was in imminent danger. But in Furious, Catherine overpowers him easily, forcing his head back to the floor. In the next scene, he is lying helpless in bed while she stands over him with a syringe.

It is a startling reversal of the way the show presented the pair only an episode earlier: him, tall, middle-aged, powerful, and physically imposing; her, young, working-class, and small enough to be almost engulfed by him. Now, his size is irrelevant. She has rendered him powerless and is deciding what will happen to his body. It is in this transformation—from apparent prey to the most dangerous person in the room—that much of the satisfaction of Furious lies.
points: “Furious” imagines a world in which the powerful can be made physically afraid of someone they once regarded as disposable.
Its popularity may tell us less about women’s appetite for brutality than about our collapsing faith in systems of justice.

articles.title: Here's What Lifehacker Readers Think Apple Will Announce on Wednesday
articles.summary: Following the third and final round of Lifehacker's Big Guessing Game, we can see what readers think Apple will announce during its big iPhone keynote next week.
body: On Wednesday, Apple will finally host its big fall event, and we will likely get our first look at the Apple Watch Series 12, iPhone 18 Pro, and iPhone Ultra, Apple's first foldable iPhone. In the lead-up to this keynote, Lifehacker ran the third and final round of our Big Guessing Game, inviting readers to make predictions about what Apple will announce this week. While we won't know the answers to those questions until Apple officially confirms them during the event, here's a look at what readers think will happen.

The rumors strongly predict that Apple will announce new iPhones and a new Apple Watch on Wednesday, but there's always the possibility of more devices as well. Apple may release new AirPods—with or without embedded cameras—and while there's a chance they'll announce new Macs, I'm skeptical, given that Apple surprised us all with Mac news last week.

articles.title: This Viral Mini Keychain Camera Is Truly Worth the Hype
articles.summary: Kodak's $35 camera captures all my favorite travel memories—and it fits in the palm of my hand.
body: One thing about me is that I always carry around a conversation starter. It makes entering a new space alone less daunting since you'll find that wherever you go, someone will walk right up to you and inevitably ask, “What is that?” Recently, for me, that's been the Kodak Charmera. Perhaps my favorite thing I've ever owned (or at the very least, my favorite thing I got this year), this tiny Kodak keychain camera is a talking point, fashion statement, and memory recorder all in one. Sure, the image quality isn't high-definition 4K, but that's part of its charm.

I first saw this camera on an Instagram reel and immediately knew I needed one. It's the perfect travel companion since it clips directly onto your bag so you'll never forget it, can be charged with a regular USB-C cord, and is primed to record your memories around the world. It may look a bit silly at first when you're holding it up to your eye to get the perfect shot, but the joy you'll get from the experience more than makes up for it.
points: Kodak's $35 camera captures all my favorite travel memories—and it fits in the palm of my hand.
